Name: Garbage In Garbage Can - Don't Hoard Trash
Author: focustense
Description:
[color=#ffdd96][size=6]Garbage In Garbage Can
[/size][/color]
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/26607/26607-1722615634-434318402.png[/img]

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Introduction[/size][/color]

For better or for worse, limited inventory space is one of Stardew Valley's important balance mechanics. A lot of games have this. It's not unusual.

What [i]is[/i] unusual, and frequently frustrating, is just how [i]quickly[/i] the trash items start to pile up in your inventory, and how very easy it is to permanently lose a valuable item by not clearing your inventory in time.

[list]
[*]Went down a staircase, possibly accidentally due to janky hitboxes? There's no backtracking, so any items left on the ground are gone.
[*]Set a bomb or used the napalm ring near an item still on the ground? Now it's gone.
[*]Near water or lava and the item's random drop trajectory placed it out of bounds, and you didn't magneto-pull it in because inventory was full? Gone.
[*]Passed out at 2 am during a dive and that super-rare weapon/shard/luck ring is just sitting there, staring at you, mocking you, and your stupid character is refusing to pick it up because apparently that nearby stack of 5 wood was more important? RAGE.
[/list]
Or perhaps this doesn't happen to you because you're meticulous about managing inventory. Perhaps you are used to the rhythm of opening the inventory menu every six seconds because you're near max capacity and every slime in the mobs you have to keep clearing each reliably drops [i]two[/i] items you have no practical use for. Perhaps menuing is [i]fun[/i] for you. Perhaps you are insane.

So what's a sane player/runner to do, other than cheat? The answer: this mod, right here. No longer will you be a slave to the trash items constantly accumulating in your backpack. Don't work for your inventory; make your inventory work for you. Insert your own slogan here.

Garbage In Garbage [Can], or GIGc, or just GIG, takes the items [i]you[/i] consider to be trash, and makes sure they never clutter up in your inventory in the first place. Enjoy a pristine backpack, completely free of useless* stacks of sap, slime, quartz crystals and dead bugs.

[size=1][i]* Yes, these items do have [/i]some[i] use, during specific parts of the game, depending on your goals and strategy. That's why [/i]you[i] get to choose what's garbage. I picked those examples because they are trash for 99% of players, 99% of the time.[/i][/size]

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Installation[/size][/color]

GIG follows the standard installation procedure for most mods:

[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI and set up your game for mods, per the [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Player_Guide/Getting_Started]Modding: Player's Guide[/url] instructions.
[*]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/28870]Stardew UI[/url].
[*]Download the main file from the Files tab.
[*]Open the .zip file and extract the [font=Courier New]GarbageInGarbageCan[/font] folder into your [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley\Mods[/font] folder.
[*]Launch the game!
[/list]
[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Optional Dependencies[/size][/color]

Configuration settings can be changed in-game using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url]. If you are one of the eight people not using GMCM, you can still use this mod and configure it using [font=Courier New]config.json[/font]. See the Configuration section for more details.

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Features & Guide[/size][/color]

GIG tries to preserve the game's balance and fit in smoothly with regular gameplay, while making inventory management less of a chore.

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Mark Items as Trash[/size][/color]

When you start a new game or first install the mod, initially your trash filter will be empty.

To add an item to the filter - that is, to designate it as trash - simply trash it the normal way, i.e. by dropping it into your trash can from the inventory menu, while holding the configured Modifier Key (default: [font=Courier New][b]LeftControl[/b][/font]). You'll see a notification:

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/flagged-notification.png[/img]

Afterward, any time you "pick up" this item, it will automatically get sent to the trash. It will still count as a pickup for the purposes of quests, mail, etc., but it will not appear in your inventory. If you haven't disabled trash notifications, you'll receive a separate notification when this happens:

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/trash-notification.png[/img]

This is the mod working as intended. You'll also be credited any money you'd get for trashing the item normally, i.e. based on your trash can's upgrade level.

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Recover Trashed Items[/size][/color]

You might run into situations where items that you intended to keep get trashed - for example, when on a fetch quest, or when pulling a large stack out of a chest. For a limited time (default: 5 seconds), you can recover these items.

To open the recovery menu, hover over the trash can in your inventory menu [b]without[/b] holding any item, like so:

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/trash-can-hover.png[/img]

Then, while holding the same Modifier Key that you use for marking items, click on the can or press the controller's action button (A). If any items are still available, you'll be presented with the recovery menu:

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/recovery-menu.png[/img]

This menu acts similar to any other container, such as a chest, but you can't put items back. Once you take an item/stack, it will go back in your inventory and you'll lose the money you were credited for trashing it.

[quote]
[b]NOTE:[/b]

The recovery process can [b]only[/b] be initiated from the inventory menu or "pause menu". If you click on the trash can in any other menu (such as a chest menu) using the modifier key, nothing will happen.[/quote]

Items recovered this way are [i]temporarily[/i] exempt from trash rules; they will not be automatically trashed the instant you try to recover them. However, they are not [i]permanently[/i] exempt. In particular any [i]new[/i] items of the same type will get trashed instead of adding to the stack; or, if you've configured Minimum Empty Slots, then the original items may get trashed again as soon as you try to pick up a different item. In either case, if you want to hold onto them and/or continue to collect more, make sure to actually mark them as non-trash after they're recovered.

If you waited too long to recover the items, or if you've disabled this feature entirely, then you won't get the recovery menu, and will instead see a notification:

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/no-recovery-notification.png[/img]

This means you've passed the point of no return; any items that were previously trashed are gone forever and cannot be recovered.

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Trash Menu[/size][/color]

The definition of trash is highly personal and highly situational; just ask Linus. By default, trash flags apply in the current location only, so you can collect wood when chopping down trees on the farm or in the forest but not when destroying crates in the mines/cavern.

Depending on the situation, you may want to do one of the following:

[list]
[*]Stop treating a particular item as trash, if you suddenly find yourself needing to collect it, e.g. for a quest; or
[*]Tag an item to be treated as trash [i]everywhere[/i], not just in the current location. For example, you might want to do this for [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Trash_(item)]Trash[/url], or other fishing trash.
[/list]
These can be done in the Trash Menu, which can be brought up by pressing the Menu Key (default [font=Courier New][b]G[/b][/font]):

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/trash-menu.png[/img]

Most of this content should be self-explanatory... but just in case:

[list]
[*]Items with [img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/trash-overlay-local-closeup.png[/img] can be auto-discarded in the player's current location. Press A (gamepad) or left-click (mouse) to toggle this.
[*]Items with [img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/trash-overlay-global-closeup.png[/img] can be auto-discarded regardless of the player's current location. Press X (gamepad) or right-click (mouse) to toggle this.
[*]If the item's icon is fully opaque, the filter is [i]active in this location[/i] - i.e. it is [i]either[/i] discardable in this location [i]or[/i] discardable in all locations. If the item's icon is translucent, it is [i]not active in this location[/i].
[/list]
[quote]
[b]NOTE:[/b]

If, as a result of your menu choices, an item is no longer considered a trash item in [i]any[/i] location, or globally, then it will disappear from the trash menu entirely the next time you open it. To make it reappear, you will have to mark it as trash again in any location.[/quote]

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Minimum Empty Slots[/size][/color]

Cautious cats may want to avoid trashing any items until they actually need the inventory space for something else (i.e. [i]non-trash[/i]). Perhaps you have a tendency to go coal farming in the mines at 11 PM when there's nothing else to do, and there's no reason to start trashing every Quartz crystal or Frozen Tear when you're not going to have a full inventory by the end of the day.

If you've decided to be a cautious cat, let GIG know by setting your Minimum Empty Slots to something other than zero:

[img]https://raw.githubusercontent.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/master/docs/images/config-menu-empty-slots.png[/img]

The way this actually works in-game is as follows:

[list]
[*]If you pick up a trash item that fully stacks with another item in your inventory - i.e. is guaranteed not to occupy a new slot - then it will always be added to that stack.
[*]If the number of empty slots in your inventory is at or below the minimum, and you are about to pick up a trash item that does [i]not[/i] stack, then the trash item will be discarded instead of picked up.
[*]If you pick up a [i]non-trash[/i] item which causes the number of empty slots to go below the minimum, [i]and[/i] you have one or more trash items already in your inventory, then those trash items in your inventory will be [i]removed from your inventory[/i] (and sent to the trash can) until you either have the required number of empty slots, or until there is no more trash left in your inventory.
[/list]
This is the more surgical solution to the originally-stated problem: "never leave a valuable item behind because of trash in the inventory" - but also don't aggressively throw out everything that's not valuable. This is closer to how a normal human would actually manage inventory, but without the endless cycle of menuing once the inventory is nearly full of valuable items.

[quote]
[b]NOTE:[/b]

There is no "trash priority" - trash is trash. When discarding trash as a result of picking up non-trash, your inventory will get searched in reverse position order, so if you really need to prioritize your trash, put the "important" trash at the top/left of your inventory.

...but really, just bring up the Trash Menu and set the item as not-trash if you want to start collecting it again. The mod is supposed to make your life easier, not harder.[/quote]

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Trash Persistence[/size][/color]

Your trash items are [i]per-save[/i], so that when you start a new game and actually need all that sap, fiber, and so on, you don't have to go into the menu and disable them.

Because the definition of trash is so context-sensitive, there is presently no "game-wide" or "default" trash list that would apply to every existing save, or every newly-created file.

Mod configuration (below) is different from trash filters, is not save-specific, and changes are applied immediately regardless of save file.

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Configuration[/size][/color]

All of this mod's options are configurable through GMCM. If you prefer to edit the [font=Courier New]config.json[/font] or are having any trouble with the in-game settings, read on for a detailed explanation of what the settings do.

[b]Example Configuration[/b]

[font=Courier New]{
  "EnableTrashNotification": true,
  "SuppressPickupNotification": true,
  "MenuKey": "G",
  "ModifierKey": "RightShoulder",
  "MinEmptySlots": 2,
  "RecoveryLimit": "00:00:05"
}[/font]

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Settings[/size][/color]

[b]These settings are global; unlike your current "trash list" or "trash filter", they are not per-save.[/b]

[list]
[*][font=Courier New]EnableTrashNotification[/font]: Whether to show a HUD notification when an item gets automatically discarded by the mod.
[*][font=Courier New]SuppressPickupNotification[/font]: Whether to suppress the item pickup notification that would normally show just [i]before[/i] the item gets trashed. It's best to leave this enabled if [font=Courier New]EnableTrashNotification[/font] is also enabled, so that you don't see two nearly-identical messages for the same item stack.
[*][font=Courier New]MenuKey[/font]: The key binding to open the trash menu, where you can enable/disable specific trash items. Unlike the GMCM page, the JSON format can accept a list, such as [font=Courier New]G, RightStick[/font], but if you want to set up controller support for the menu, you're better off using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/25257]Radial Menu[/url].
[*][font=Courier New]ModifierKey[/font]: The key to [b]hold[/b] while trashing an item to mark it as trash, or while clicking on the trash can without any held item to bring up the recovery menu. In the example above, it's been changed from the default [font=Courier New]LeftControl[/font] to [font=Courier New]RightShoulder[/font] to work with gamepads.
[*][font=Courier New]MinEmptySlots[/font]: Number of empty inventory slots to try to maintain. Default is [font=Courier New]0[/font] which turns this feature off; in the example above, we've chosen [font=Courier New]2[/font], which will only trash items when the inventory reaches 2 slots or fewer.
[*][font=Courier New]RecoveryLimit[/font]: Maximum amount of time before trashed items disappear forever and can no longer be recovered via the recovery menu (see [font=Courier New]ModifierKey[/font] above). The example above uses the default limit of 5 seconds. Note that this is in [b]real[/b] seconds, not in-game time; however, the counter only counts down while your character is in-play, so items won't disappear while the game is paused, in the middle of a dialogue/cutscene, etc.
[/list]

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Frequently Unasked Questions[/size][/color]

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]What's with the name?[/size][/color]

It's a [url=https://freeimage.host/i/dA6mk9R]Simpsons reference[/url]. (Context: [url=https://frinkiac.com/caption/S07E03/793175]S07E03[/url])

I was originally going to call it "AutoTrash", and you might still see that name in one or two dark corners of the code repo. Then I found out there was already a mod with that name. It's 5 years old, has never been updated, and from what I can tell, may never have worked properly in the first place. This one works. At least, it Works On My Machine™.

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Couldn't I just use a mod that gives me a huge/infinite backpack?[/size][/color]

Sure. That is what we in the business call "cheating". Stardew Valley is a single-player/co-op game, so knock yourself out if that's more appealing to you. GIG is for the players who want to keep the same difficulty but eliminate the constant micromanagement.

Also, with a bigger backpack, you'd still [i]eventually[/i] have to decide what to do with all that trash; it's just delaying the inevitable.

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Okay, but couldn't I use a mod like Chests Anywhere to send all that trash away?[/size][/color]

What did I [i]just[/i] say?

Also, those mods won't stop your inventory from filling up, they just give you a different place to (manually) move your trash to.

[color=#fff2cc][size=4]Why do you hate sap? What did sap ever do to you?[/size][/color]

It's the quintessential "trash but not trash haha" item. It [i]has[/i] a sell value, it's just pathetically low; it's consumable, but has only negative effects; it's a common drop from a common monster present in nearly every location; it has virtually no utility in crafting except for a couple of late-game recipes that are highly constrained by [i]other[/i] ingredients; and aside from that very first time you sell it to Pierre and hear the townspeople's commentary, it doesn't even have meme value like the Skyrim bucket. In every run, I find it [i]constantly[/i] wasting valuable inventory space.

Even algae/seaweed items are marginally useful, e.g. in cooking or some buildings, even if they're not worth the animation frames required to eat them once you hit your midgame stride. Sap is trash 99% of the time.

[color=#ffe599][size=5]Questions/Bugs?[/size][/color]

Feel free to either:

[list][*]Create a [url=https://github.com/focustense/StardewAutoTrash/issues]GitHub issue[/url]; when doing so, please follow bug-reporting etiquette. Check first for similar reports, and make sure to include all relevant details about your issue, especially including clear repro steps and/or [url=https://smapi.io/log]SMAPI log[/url].
[*]Or, ping me on the [url=https://discord.com/invite/stardewvalley]SV Discord[/url] if I happen to be around. Discord is best if you have a quick question, but I make no promises re: availability for in-depth troubleshooting. [i](DMs will be ignored.)[/i]
[/list]
As is my policy, comments/posts on Nexus will always be open so that community members can support each other when I’m on modding hiatus, but I will probably not see them nor respond. GitHub and Discord are my only two communication channels.
